Principle 01 of 8

Honesty

Tell people the truth about prices, products, services, and claims.

Protects

Customers, the public

Why it matters

People can only decide well on accurate information. Deception takes money and trust from people who never agreed to give them.

Covers

Pricing and billing (Category 1), marketing and capability claims (Category 7), sneaking and urgency patterns (3.1–3.2), misleading privacy and authority claims (5.3, 5.5), and AI misrepresentation (6.4).

1.1 Hidden Costs & Drip Pricing · 6 practices

Honesty
§PracticeDescriptionSeen in
1.1.1Drip PricingAdvertising a base price while progressively revealing mandatory fees during checkout, so the final total far exceeds the price the user committed to.Airlines (baggage, seat fees), hotels (resort fees), event ticketing, e-commerce, travel
1.1.2Hidden Mandatory FeesAdding non-optional service, facility, processing, regulatory, or "amenity" fees not disclosed alongside the headline price.Hospitality, ride-hailing, telecom, fitness, real estate (junk fees), wedding planning
1.1.3Sneak-into-BasketAuto-adding items, insurance, warranties, donations, or services to a cart that the user must explicitly remove.E-commerce, travel booking, ticketing, financial services
1.1.4Hidden Surcharges & StackingLayering numerous small fees (fuel, residential, peak, accessorial) so the final invoice is opaque even to attentive customers.Shipping & freight, food delivery, logistics, waste management, energy utilities
1.1.5Foreign Transaction OpacityBurying currency-conversion markups or international fees in fine print rather than disclosing at point of sale.Financial services, travel & tourism
1.1.6Dynamic-Currency Conversion MarkupOffering on-the-fly currency conversion at unfavorable rates without disclosing the markup, so users unwittingly pay above-market exchange.Travel & tourism, payment processing

1.2 Surge & Crisis Pricing · 5 practices

Honesty+ Care
§PracticeDescriptionSeen in
1.2.1Crisis-Period Price GougingAlgorithmically raising prices on essential goods or services during emergencies, weather events, or supply shocks when consumers cannot defer purchase.Grocery, e-commerce, ride-hailing, food delivery, plumbing/home repair, pest control
1.2.2Emergency-Markup ExploitationCharging premium rates for after-hours, urgent, or emergency service when the customer has no time to compare alternatives.Plumbing, automotive towing, veterinary, healthcare, funeral services, cybersecurity (ransomware response)
1.2.3Last-Minute Price InflationRaising prices dramatically as the deadline (travel date, event, deadline) approaches, exploiting urgency.Travel, ticketing, gambling, betting
1.2.4Algorithmic Personalized PricingAdjusting prices in real time based on browsing history, device, location, or perceived willingness to pay without disclosure.Hospitality, e-commerce, ride-hailing, grocery, fashion, ticketing
1.2.5Tourist-Targeted OverchargingCharging higher prices to visibly identifiable visitors who lack local knowledge of fair prices, sometimes refusing meters or quoting opaque flat rates.Taxi services, retail in tourist zones, hospitality, currency exchange

1.3 Bait-and-Switch Pricing · 7 practices

Honesty
§PracticeDescriptionSeen in
1.3.1Bait PricingAdvertising a price or product that is unavailable, then steering the customer to a more expensive alternative.Real estate, automotive sales, e-commerce, cleaning services, home services
1.3.2Yo-Yo FinancingLetting a customer take possession after a sale, then claiming financing fell through to impose worse terms.Automotive
1.3.3Underbid-and-InflateSubmitting a low bid to win a contract, then recovering margin through change orders, "unforeseen conditions," or scope creep.Construction, home services, plumbing, consulting
1.3.4Allowance UnderspecificationSetting unrealistically low material or service allowances in a quote, knowing the customer will exceed them and pay the difference.Construction, home services, wedding planning
1.3.5Diagnostic-to-Repair ConversionAdvertising free or low-cost diagnostics that convert into expensive repair commitments without re-quoting.Plumbing, automotive repair, pest control
1.3.6Vendor SubstitutionReplacing the contracted vendor or specified material with a lower-cost alternative while charging the original rate.Wedding planning, construction, dental (lab work), beauty (formulation)
1.3.7Renewal-Time Feature DowngradeRemoving or restricting features included in the prior term and offering them only at a higher tier upon renewal.Cloud / SaaS, streaming, mobile carriers, fitness

1.4 Markup Concealment & Junk Fees · 12 practices

Honesty
§PracticeDescriptionSeen in
1.4.1Material/Parts Markup ConcealmentCharging retail or inflated prices for materials, parts, or supplies while presenting prices as "at cost" or omitting markup disclosure.Plumbing, home services, dental (lab work), veterinary, cleaning, automotive repair
1.4.2Apprentice-at-Journeyman RateBilling senior-level rates while assigning the work to junior, unqualified, or apprentice personnel.Consulting, legal services, plumbing, accounting & auditing
1.4.3Billable-Hour InflationPadding hours through unnecessary meetings, redundant research, or rounded entries.Consulting, legal services, accounting & auditing
1.4.4Expense PaddingInflating travel, accommodation, and operational expenses passed through to clients beyond actual cost.Consulting, legal services
1.4.5Flat-Rate Pricing OpacityQuoting flat rates that vastly exceed the time-and-materials cost without disclosing the calculation, hiding effective hourly rates.Plumbing, home services, automotive repair
1.4.6Mini-Bar / Incidentals GougingCharging extreme markups (often 300–800%) on captive in-room or in-venue items, sometimes with sensor-based auto-billing for items merely moved.Hotels, event venues, hospitality, pet industry (in-clinic prescriptions)
1.4.7Wedding/Occasion TaxCharging more for identical services when labeled with a high-emotion event (wedding, funeral) than for an ordinary "event."Wedding planning, funeral services
1.4.8MSRP Inflation for Discount IllusionSetting artificially high "manufacturer suggested retail prices" so retailers can advertise large but illusory discounts.Home appliances, fashion, e-commerce
1.4.9Outlet-Store DeceptionManufacturing lower-quality goods specifically for outlet channels while implying they are excess or overstock from the main line.Fashion & apparel
1.4.10Captive-Venue Concession MarkupCharging extreme markups on essential items (food, water, basic snacks) inside venues where consumers cannot leave and return, often selling commodity items at 5–10× retail.Theme parks, sports stadiums, concert venues, cinemas, airports (post-security), cruise ships
1.4.11Outside-Food / Drink ProhibitionBanning patrons from bringing essential items (water, food, baby formula) into a venue specifically to channel demand into overpriced concessions, sometimes confiscating items at entry.Theme parks, sports stadiums, concert venues, cinemas
1.4.12Cultural-Practice Pricing-OutInflating prices on items central to a society's customary rituals (shared meals, gathering venues, holiday foods) well beyond cost basis, making the cultural practice economically inaccessible while continuing to market the venue or product as part of that ritual.Restaurants (American social-eating culture), event venues, holiday-food retail, "third place" cafes

Honesty+ Fairness
§PracticeDescriptionSeen in

§PracticeDescriptionSeen in
